claims.text: A predictive framework using local chemical-environment descriptors can identify high-entropy alloys with exceptionally low phonon thermal conductivity.
The proposed framework will be at least 20% more accurate than current methods.
Compositional complexity produces short-range lattice distortions in high-entropy alloys.
Short-range lattice distortions strongly scatter phonons.
The intended materials are equiatomic or near-equiatomic, single-phase FCC or BCC high-entropy alloys without significant secondary phases.
Local-environment descriptors can capture atomic-level disorder in candidate high-entropy alloys.
Short-range lattice distortions and chemical disorder reduce phonon mean free path.
A reduced phonon mean free path lowers phonon thermal conductivity.
Descriptors quantifying local structural complexity capture phonon scattering from chemical and lattice disorder more effectively than standard methods.
More effective representation of disorder-induced phonon scattering leads to improved predictive performance.
The approach will achieve 20% higher accuracy than state-of-the-art methods in identifying low-phonon-thermal-conductivity compositions.
The approach will predict at least a 10% reduction in thermal conductivity for newly identified compositions relative to standard references.
Current DFT- and classical force-field-based methods for high-entropy alloys commonly rely on averaged structural properties.
The approach is expected to be accurate mainly for near-equiatomic, single-phase high-entropy alloys with stable FCC or BCC structures.
The approach may be less reliable for alloys with two-phase regions, secondary precipitates, or strongly off-stoichiometric compositions.
Complex phase transformations and severe off-stoichiometry may degrade predictive accuracy.
Limited data for new compositions may reduce training reliability.
